rows.statement: 21-day window: The three-week period a player designated to return from injured reserve has, once he begins practicing, to be activated to the roster or else stay on reserve for the season.

sources.citation: NFL Injury Report Explained: History, Rules, and Designations (WebMD)
sources.quote: Once an eligible player is designated to return and begins practicing, the team has a 21-day window to activate him.

sources.citation: NFL roster designations explained (AP via FOX Sports) (FOX Sports (Associated Press))
sources.quote: it activates a 21-day window during which the player must be activated to the 53-man roster

rows.notes: FOX/AP (2023) says players must miss four games and up to eight can be designated; WebMD adds two more for playoff teams under the 2026 framework.

rows.statement: Active/Inactive list: The game-day split of a club's roster into players available to play and players not dressed; a club's active/inactive list may not exceed 53 players, and inactives are announced about 90 minutes before kickoff.

sources.citation: NFL-NFLPA Collective Bargaining Agreement 2020, Article 25 (Squad Size) (NFL-NFLPA CBA)
sources.quote: a Club's Active/Inactive List shall not exceed 53 players

sources.citation: NFL Injury Report Explained: History, Rules, and Designations (WebMD)
sources.quote: The inactive list is generally released 90 minutes before kickoff.

rows.notes: CBA active list limit is 48 players (47 if fewer than eight offensive linemen); 54 or 55 total only with practice-squad elevations.

rows.statement: ATC spotter: A certified athletic trainer in a stadium booth with video access who watches the game for injuries, radios the club's medical staff and referee, and can call a medical timeout.

sources.citation: NFL-NFLPA Collective Bargaining Agreement 2020, Appendix W (NFL Head, Neck and Spine Committee's Concussion Diagnosis and Management Protocol) (NFL-NFLPA CBA)
sources.quote: Two certified athletic trainers will be assigned to a stadium booth with access to multiple views of video

sources.citation: NFL Football Operations: Football terms (NFL Football Operations)
sources.quote: Independent Certified Athletic Trainers called ATC spotters can also stop the game if it appears a player is injured

sources.citation: Concussion Protocol & Return-to-Participation Protocol: Overview (NFL)
sources.quote: booth ATC spotter

rows.notes: Spotters are connected by radio to the on-field officials as well as medical staffs (CBA Appendix W). NFL fact-sheet quote is a naming reference only.

rows.statement: Cleared: A physician's release stating that a player may take part in practice or games; under the CBA the Head Team Physician has final authority, and a concussed player also needs the independent consultant's confirmation.

sources.citation: NFL-NFLPA Collective Bargaining Agreement 2020, Article 39 (Players' Rights to Medical Care and Treatment) Sec. 1(d) (NFL-NFLPA CBA)
sources.quote: exclusive and final authority to determine whether a player is cleared to return to participation

sources.citation: Concussion Protocol & Return-to-Participation Protocol: Overview (NFL)
sources.quote: After a player has progressed through the five-step process, and is cleared for full participation by his club physician

sources.citation: NFL roster designations explained (AP via FOX Sports) (FOX Sports (Associated Press))
sources.quote: can be activated at any point during camp when they are medically cleared

rows.statement: Concussion: A traumatic brain injury caused by biomechanical forces, usually from a blow to the head or body that sends force to the head, with a brief change in brain function that often shows nothing on standard imaging.

sources.citation: NFL-NFLPA Collective Bargaining Agreement 2020, Appendix W (NFL Head, Neck and Spine Committee's Concussion Diagnosis and Management Protocol) (NFL-NFLPA CBA)
sources.quote: Sports related concussion ("SRC") is a traumatic brain injury induced by biomechanical forces.

rows.notes: Only the CBA appendix (adapted by the NFL from McCrory et al., BJSM 2017) was read so far; a second and third medical publisher are still needed (see summary).

rows.statement: Concussion protocol: The league-mandated steps for evaluating a possible concussion during a game (sideline and locker-room exams, with independent consultants and spotters involved) and for managing the player afterward.

sources.citation: NFL-NFLPA Collective Bargaining Agreement 2020, Appendix W (NFL Head, Neck and Spine Committee's Concussion Diagnosis and Management Protocol) (NFL-NFLPA CBA)
sources.quote: developed a comprehensive set of protocols regarding the diagnosis and management of concussions in NFL players

sources.citation: Concussion Protocol & Return-to-Participation Protocol: Overview (NFL)
sources.quote: developed the NFL Game Day Concussion Diagnosis and Management Protocol in 2011

sources.citation: NFL concussion protocol explained: Symptoms, evaluation, return to play (NBC Sports)
sources.quote: The game-day concussion protocol was first released in 2011.

rows.notes: NFL and NFLPA changed the checklist in 2022 to add ataxia as a 'no-go' sign (NBC; NFL fact sheet describes 2018 changes). The CBA text on file is the 2020 version of Appendix W.

rows.statement: Did not participate: An injury-report practice status meaning the player did not take part in practice that day.

sources.citation: NFL Injury Report Explained: History, Rules, and Designations (WebMD)
sources.quote: Did Not Participate (DNP): The player did not take part in practice.

rows.notes: WebMD is the only source read for the DNP/LP/FP triplet; the NFL's own policy text was not reachable.

rows.statement: Doubtful: A game-status designation meaning the player is unlikely to play.

sources.citation: NFL Injury Report Explained: History, Rules, and Designations (WebMD)
sources.quote: Doubtful: The player is unlikely to play.

rows.notes: Before 2016 'doubtful' was defined as about a 25 percent chance of playing (WebMD).

rows.statement: Full participation: An injury-report practice status meaning the player completed his normal practice workload.

sources.citation: NFL Injury Report Explained: History, Rules, and Designations (WebMD)
sources.quote: Full Participation (FP): The player completed his normal practice workload.

rows.notes: Single publisher so far.

rows.statement: Game status: The injury-report entry that tells the public whether each injured player is expected to play in the club's next game: out, doubtful or questionable.

sources.citation: NFL Injury Report Explained: History, Rules, and Designations (WebMD)
sources.quote: The Game Status Report identifies whether he is expected to play.

rows.notes: Single publisher so far.

rows.statement: In-game injury reporting: The rule that clubs must promptly and accurately announce injuries during a game, naming the body part and updating the player's status.

sources.citation: NFL Media Access Policy (2026), hosted by PFWA (NFL (Media Access Policy via PFWA))
sources.quote: In-game injury announcements must be specific to a body part, accurate, and updated as warranted

sources.citation: NFL Injury Report Explained: History, Rules, and Designations (WebMD)
sources.quote: If a player leaves the game with an injury, the team must provide accurate information about the affected body part

rows.notes: PFWA text is the NFL's Media Access Policy; clubs enter in-game injuries through the league's online Injury Reporting Platform.

rows.statement: Independent neurological consultant: A neurology-trained physician with no team affiliation, designated by each club at the start of the league year, who must examine and confirm a concussed player's clearance before he returns to contact practice or play.

sources.citation: NFL-NFLPA Collective Bargaining Agreement 2020, Appendix W (NFL Head, Neck and Spine Committee's Concussion Diagnosis and Management Protocol) (NFL-NFLPA CBA)
sources.quote: The Independent Neurological Consultant (INC) must be impartial and independent from the player's club

sources.citation: Concussion Protocol & Return-to-Participation Protocol: Overview (NFL)
sources.quote: he must be seen and separately cleared by an Independent Neurological Consultant (INC)

sources.citation: NFL concussion protocol explained: Symptoms, evaluation, return to play (NBC Sports)
sources.quote: Every NFL team is required to have at least one INC

sources.citation: NFL Media Access Policy (2026), hosted by PFWA (NFL (Media Access Policy via PFWA))
sources.quote: extends until the player has been cleared by the Independent Neurological Consultant (INC)

rows.notes: A UNC may also serve as an INC, but neither may be affiliated with an NFL team (CBA Appendix W Sec. IV). Not to be confused with UNC.

rows.statement: Injury report: The league's required weekly public report of injured players' practice participation and game status, submitted by clubs Wednesday through Friday for a Sunday game.

sources.citation: NFL Injury Report Explained: History, Rules, and Designations (WebMD)
sources.quote: The Practice Report tells the public how much an injured player took part during the week.

sources.citation: NFL Media Access Policy (2026), hosted by PFWA (NFL (Media Access Policy via PFWA))
sources.quote: issue to local media the names of those players who missed any portion of 11-on-11 team or individual work

rows.notes: WebMD says the report dates to 1947 (Bert Bell, gambling concerns). WebMD says the public gets only the body part or condition, practice participation and expected availability, not a diagnosis or timetable.

rows.statement: Injury settlement: An agreement under which a club releases an injured player and pays him some of his salary instead of carrying him on injured reserve.

sources.citation: NFL roster designations explained (AP via FOX Sports) (FOX Sports (Associated Press))
sources.quote: release him with an injury settlement

sources.citation: NFL-NFLPA Collective Bargaining Agreement 2020, Article 12 / Benefit Plan (Plan Sec. 2.1 coverage language) (NFL-NFLPA CBA)
sources.quote: paid all or part of his salary for such season pursuant to an Injury Settlement Waiver or an Injury Grievance

rows.notes: Definition is inferred from how the sources use the term; no source gave a full definition in one sentence. Needs a third publisher (for example Over The Cap).

rows.statement: Limited participation: An injury-report practice status meaning the player took part but fewer than all of his normal practice reps.

sources.citation: NFL Injury Report Explained: History, Rules, and Designations (WebMD)
sources.quote: Limited Participation (LP): The player took fewer than 100% of his normal practice repetitions.

rows.notes: Single publisher so far.

rows.statement: Medical care and treatment: The CBA article that governs player medical care: club physician and trainer credentials, the right to a second opinion and to choose a surgeon, and concussion protocol enforcement.

sources.citation: NFL-NFLPA Collective Bargaining Agreement 2020, Article 39 (Players' Rights to Medical Care and Treatment) (NFL-NFLPA CBA)
sources.quote: Each Club will have a board-certified orthopedic surgeon as one of its Club physicians

rows.notes: Single primary text; a CBA article title rather than a football term in common use.

rows.statement: Medical timeout: A stoppage called through the referee at the request of the booth ATC spotter when a player who appears to need concussion evaluation is about to stay in the game without being checked.

sources.citation: NFL-NFLPA Collective Bargaining Agreement 2020, Appendix W (NFL Head, Neck and Spine Committee's Concussion Diagnosis and Management Protocol) (NFL-NFLPA CBA)
sources.quote: the Booth ATC Spotter is required to call a Medical Time-Out to assure the concussion evaluation occurs

sources.citation: NFL Football Operations: Football terms (NFL Football Operations)
sources.quote: ATC spotters can also stop the game if it appears a player is injured

rows.notes: The NFL's football-terms page calls these 'injury timeouts' when called by officials or spotters; a different, official-called injury timeout also exists for ordinary injuries.

rows.statement: Out (injury report designation): A game-status designation meaning the player will not play.

sources.citation: NFL Injury Report Explained: History, Rules, and Designations (WebMD)
sources.quote: Out: The player will not play.

rows.notes: Not an offense term: belongs with injury reporting. Only WebMD found in this pass (the ESPN page cited by the drafting agent did not show its article text). Flag: single publisher.

rows.statement: Out (injury report): A game-status designation meaning the player will not play.

sources.citation: NFL Injury Report Explained: History, Rules, and Designations (WebMD)
sources.quote: Out: The player will not play.

rows.notes: Added: the draft listed Questionable, Doubtful and Probable but not Out, the third current game-status category.

rows.statement: Physical examination: The medical exam club doctors give each player on report day to camp and before minicamps; the CBA sets a standard minimum preseason exam.

sources.citation: NFL-NFLPA Collective Bargaining Agreement 2020, Appendix K (Standard Minimum Preseason Physical Examination) (NFL-NFLPA CBA)
sources.quote: STANDARD MINIMUM PRESEASON PHYSICAL EXAMINATION

rows.notes: Single primary text.

rows.statement: Probable: A former game-status designation meaning the player was likely to play (generally at least 75 percent); the NFL eliminated it in 2016.

sources.citation: NFL Injury Report Explained: History, Rules, and Designations (WebMD)
sources.quote: In 2016, the NFL eliminated the category.

rows.notes: Single publisher so far.

rows.statement: Questionable: A game-status designation meaning it is uncertain whether the player will play.

sources.citation: NFL Injury Report Explained: History, Rules, and Designations (WebMD)
sources.quote: Questionable: It is uncertain whether the player will play.

rows.notes: Before 2016 'questionable' meant roughly 50-50 (WebMD).

rows.statement: Return-to-participation protocol: The five-step graduated program a concussed player must pass before full practice or play: rest and recovery, light aerobic exercise, continued aerobic exercise with strength training, football-specific non-contact activity, then full football activity and clearance.

sources.citation: NFL-NFLPA Collective Bargaining Agreement 2020, Appendix W (NFL Head, Neck and Spine Committee's Concussion Diagnosis and Management Protocol) (NFL-NFLPA CBA)
sources.quote: Step One: Rest and Recovery

sources.citation: Concussion Protocol & Return-to-Participation Protocol: Overview (NFL)
sources.quote: must follow a five-step process before being cleared to fully practice or participate in an NFL game

sources.citation: NFL concussion protocol explained: Symptoms, evaluation, return to play (NBC Sports)
sources.quote: the protocol outlines five phases, beginning with symptom limited activity

rows.notes: Steps in the CBA appendix: Step Two Light Aerobic Exercise; Step Three Continued Aerobic Exercise and Introduction of Strength Training; Step Four Football Specific Activities. NBC's wording of the first phase ('symptom limited activity') differs from the CBA's 'Rest and Recovery'. There is no set timeframe; the club physician decides and the INC must confirm clearance.

rows.statement: Return to play: The graded process, and the physician's decision, by which an injured player goes back to practice and games.

sources.citation: NFL-NFLPA Collective Bargaining Agreement 2020, Appendix W (NFL Head, Neck and Spine Committee's Concussion Diagnosis and Management Protocol) (NFL-NFLPA CBA)
sources.quote: remains within the professional judgment of the Head Team Physician or team physician designated for concussion evaluation

sources.citation: Concussion Protocol & Return-to-Participation Protocol: Overview (NFL)
sources.quote: there is no set time-frame for return to participation

rows.notes: Draft row had a generic definition; sources here are concussion-specific, general injury return-to-play is governed by the Head Team Physician under Art. 39 Sec. 1(d).

rows.statement: Second opinion: A player's right to have another board-certified physician examine him; the club pays only if the player consults the club physician first and the second doctor reports back to him.

sources.citation: NFL-NFLPA Collective Bargaining Agreement 2020, Article 39 (Players' Rights to Medical Care and Treatment) Sec. 6 (NFL-NFLPA CBA)
sources.quote: A player will have the opportunity to obtain a second medical opinion.

rows.notes: Single primary text.

rows.statement: Team doctor: A physician retained by the club to treat players; each club must have a board-certified orthopedic surgeon and a primary-care sports medicine physician, one of whom is the Head Team Physician with final say on clearance.

sources.citation: NFL-NFLPA Collective Bargaining Agreement 2020, Article 39 (Players' Rights to Medical Care and Treatment) Sec. 1(a) (NFL-NFLPA CBA)
sources.quote: Each Club will have a board-certified orthopedic surgeon as one of its Club physicians

sources.citation: Training camp (NFL) - Wikipedia (Wikipedia)
sources.quote: every team must have the team doctor and trainers on the field

rows.notes: Wikipedia's field-presence sentence is tied to training-camp heat concerns after the 2001 death of Korey Stringer.

rows.statement: Unaffiliated neurotrauma consultant: An independent physician with no club affiliation, assigned by the league to each game to help spot and evaluate possible head injuries; two stand on the sidelines and a third watches video from the booth.

sources.citation: NFL-NFLPA Collective Bargaining Agreement 2020, Appendix W (NFL Head, Neck and Spine Committee's Concussion Diagnosis and Management Protocol) (NFL-NFLPA CBA)
sources.quote: each team will be assigned a Sideline Unaffiliated Neurotrauma Consultant

sources.citation: Concussion Protocol & Return-to-Participation Protocol: Overview (NFL)
sources.quote: Added a third UNC who will monitor the broadcast video and audio feeds of each game

sources.citation: NFL concussion protocol explained: Symptoms, evaluation, return to play (NBC Sports)
sources.quote: Three medical experts, known as unaffiliated neurotrauma consultants (UNCs), are assigned to each game

rows.notes: The UNC assists; the diagnosis and the return-to-game decision remain with the Head Team Physician or the physician managing traumatic brain injury (CBA Appendix W). The Booth UNC is separate from the Booth ATC Spotter. | Other batch definition: An independent physician assigned to each NFL game to help check head-injury evaluations; three per game (two on the sideline, one in the booth).

rows.statement: Waived/injured: A designation on an injured player who is waived: another team may claim him, or, if unclaimed, he goes onto his original team's injured reserve (or the team releases him with an injury settlement).

sources.citation: Glossary of American football - Wikipedia (Wikipedia)
sources.quote: If the waived/injured player is not claimed by another team, then they are placed on the injured reserve

sources.citation: NFL roster designations explained (AP via FOX Sports) (FOX Sports (Associated Press))
sources.quote: waived/injured, which means the player can be claimed by another team or revert to his original team's IR list

rows.notes: Wikipedia ties the rule to non-vested veterans before the cutdown to 53; FOX/AP describes it more generally.
